payload.title: Add secure login to this application.

contract.goal: Implement secure login endpoints for this application, reusing the existing user model and session store
constraints: Reuse the existing SessionStore and UserRepo; do not add a database
Do not add new paid infrastructure or external services
Keep all changes covered by vitest tests under tests/auth/

acceptance_criteria.condition: A valid login credential creates a user session and GET /me returns the user
An expired login credential is rejected with HTTP 401
A login credential cannot be reused after its first successful use
Changes stay within the allowed scope
The whole test suite still passes

contract.goal: Add a minimal login page that submits an email address to the backend login endpoint and shows the result
constraints: Plain HTML and vanilla JavaScript only; no framework, no build step; create the public/ directory if it does not exist
The page must call POST /auth/request with a JSON body {"email": "..."} and display the response message

acceptance_criteria.condition: public/login.html exists and contains a form posting an email to /auth/request
Changes stay within the allowed scope

interpretation: Add passwordless email login: POST /auth/login takes an email, and when it matches a user in the existing UserRepo, generates a random login token, stores only its hash with an expiry in a new in-memory LoginTokenStore under src/auth/, and sends the token via the existing EmailSender abstraction (MemoryEmailSender by default).

Add POST /auth/verify that consumes the token: a valid, unexpired, never-used token creates a session in the existing SessionStore, sets an HttpOnly SameSite cookie with the session id, and returns the user; an expired, unknown, or already-used token is rejected with HTTP 401 and the token is never accepted again.

Replace the fixed 401 on GET /me with a real lookup: read the session cookie, look the session up in SessionStore, and return the user or the existing 401 body; add POST /auth/logout that revokes the session and clears the cookie.

Wire everything in src/app.ts through an options object with injectable UserRepo, SessionStore, LoginTokenStore, EmailSender and clock so tests are hermetic; no database, no external services, no frontend changes.

Cover all of this with vitest tests under tests/auth/, including tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts and tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts as named by the acceptance checks, plus a single-use test and token-store unit tests.
assumptions: Because the User model has no password and an email sender is listed as an input, 'login credential' means a single-use, time-limited login token delivered by email (magic link / one-time code), not a password.
The login request endpoint responds identically for known and unknown emails (202 Accepted) to avoid account enumeration; the email is only sent for known users.
Login tokens expire after 15 minutes and sessions after 24 hours by default; both are configurable through createApp options.
The session is carried in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie named 'session'; the Secure flag is enabled only outside test/development to keep tests over plain HTTP working.

src/server.ts is outside allowed paths, so createApp() must keep working with zero arguments; the existing tests/app.test.ts expectation that GET /me without a session returns 401 {error:'not authenticated'} is preserved.
Tests never depend on wall-clock time; the clock is injected into all stores.
risks: The verify endpoint is the only place where token consumption happens; if consumption were not atomic with validation a token could be reused, so the token store marks a token used before creating the session and this is tested explicitly.
Hono's cookie helpers are used; the Set-Cookie format must be parsed correctly in tests when replaying the cookie on GET /me.
No rate limiting is added to POST /auth/login; with the in-memory email stub this is acceptable for the demo but should be noted for production.

verification_plan.AC-1: Write tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts: request a login for a seeded email, read the token from the MemoryEmailSender, POST it to /auth/verify, assert 200 with the user and a Set-Cookie header, then GET /me with that cookie and assert 200 with the same user. Run: npx vitest run tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts and confirm it passes.
verification_plan.AC-2: Write tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts with an injected mutable clock: request a token, advance the clock past the token TTL, POST /auth/verify and assert HTTP 401 with an error body and no session cookie; also assert GET /me stays 401. Run: npx vitest run tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts and confirm it passes.
verification_plan.AC-3: Write tests/auth/single-use.test.ts: verify the same token twice and assert the second call returns 401 and sets no cookie; also unit-test LoginTokenStore.consume returning undefined on the second call. Run those tests and include the token-store code (hash at rest, delete-on-consume) in the summary for human review.
verification_plan.AC-4: Only create or edit files under src/auth/**, src/app.ts and tests/auth/**; before submitting run git status and git diff --stat and confirm every changed path is inside the allowed list.
verification_plan.AC-5: Run npx vitest run (whole suite) and npm run typecheck and confirm both exit 0 with all existing tests, including tests/app.test.ts, still passing.

payload.message: Contract accepted. Plan: passwordless email login token (single-use, expiring, hashed at rest) in src/auth/, POST /auth/login, POST /auth/verify, POST /auth/logout, real GET /me via session cookie. Writing failing tests first.

Implementation done and checks green: 44 tests across 9 files pass (npx vitest run), tsc --noEmit clean. tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts (8), expired-login.test.ts (5), single-use.test.ts (3), login-token-store.test.ts (8) all pass. Changed paths: src/auth/login-tokens.ts, src/auth/routes.ts, src/app.ts, tests/auth/*. Submitting evidence.

AC-1.note: npx vitest run tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts: 8 tests passed. POST /auth/login emails a token, POST /auth/verify creates a SessionStore session, sets HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie and returns the user; GET /me with that cookie returns the user.

AC-2.note: npx vitest run tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts: 5 tests passed. With an injected clock advanced past the 15-minute token TTL, /auth/verify returns 401 {error:'invalid or expired login token'} and sets no cookie; boundary at exact expiry still accepted; session expiry also covered.

AC-3.note: For human review: LoginTokenStore.consume (src/auth/login-tokens.ts) deletes the token hash before returning, so validation and consumption are one step; tests/auth/single-use.test.ts (3 tests) proves a second use returns 401 while the first session stays valid, and login-token-store.test.ts proves consume returns undefined on second call. Only SHA-256 hashes are stored at rest; tokens are 32 random bytes.

AC-4.note: git diff --stat main...HEAD lists only src/app.ts, src/auth/login-tokens.ts, src/auth/routes.ts and tests/auth/{helpers,login-token-store.test,valid-login.test,expired-login.test,single-use.test}.ts. src/server.ts untouched; createApp() still works with zero args. No frontend, OAuth or password-reset changes.

AC-5.note: npx vitest run: 9 files, 44 tests passed (existing tests/app.test.ts 401 expectation on GET /me preserved). npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit) clean.

submission.summary: Passwordless email login committed as a0fc9a3 on relay/t-backend-auth. New src/auth/login-tokens.ts: LoginTokenStore with injected clock, 32-byte random base64url tokens, SHA-256 hash stored at rest, single-use consume-and-delete, expiry check. New src/auth/routes.ts: POST /auth/login (zod-validated email, identical 202 for known/unknown emails to prevent enumeration, sends token via EmailSender), POST /auth/verify (consumes token, creates session in existing SessionStore, sets HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax/Secure-outside-dev-test cookie, 401 on invalid/expired/reused), POST /auth/logout (revokes session, clears cookie). src/app.ts: createApp now takes an options object with injectable UserRepo, SessionStore, LoginTokenStore, EmailSender, clock and TTLs; GET /me resolves the session cookie. Tests under tests/auth/ (24 new) plus all existing tests pass; typecheck clean. Note: no rate limiting on /auth/login (out of scope for demo).

payload.observed_failure: Manual test: after a successful POST /auth/verify with a token, replaying the exact same token a second time returned 200 and created a second session; expected 401 and no new session.

repair.observed_failure: AC-3: Manual test: after a successful POST /auth/verify with a token, replaying the exact same token a second time returned 200 and created a second session; expected 401 and no new session.
repair.requested_correction: Make the following criteria pass without touching unrelated code: A login credential cannot be reused after its first successful use

payload.reason: Repair r1 (AC-3) reports that replaying a consumed token returned 200 and created a second session. I cannot reproduce this: sequential replay returns 200 then 401; five concurrent replays return exactly one 200 and four 401; whitespace/url-encoded variants return 401 (script run against createApp() from the committed a0fc9a3). LoginTokenStore.consume deletes the hash before any session is created. I am adding stronger regression tests (session creation counted, replay via the real src/server.ts fetch handler, concurrent replay) and resubmitting, but exact reproduction steps from the reviewer (client used, how the token was obtained, whether the same server process handled both requests) would let me pinpoint any real gap.
payload.waiting_on: human reviewer: exact reproduction steps for the AC-3 token replay observation

payload.reason: codex config fixed; will rerun in the next mission

payload.message: Repair r1 (AC-3): replay could not be reproduced locally (sequential 200/401, concurrent 1x200+4x401). Added two regression tests in tests/auth/single-use.test.ts asserting SessionStore.create is called exactly once across 5 sequential and 5 concurrent replays and only one response sets a cookie. Full suite 46/46, typecheck clean. Resubmitting.

AC-1.note: Unchanged. npx vitest run tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts: 8 passed.

AC-2.note: Unchanged. npx vitest run tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts: 5 passed.

AC-3.note: Could NOT reproduce the reported replay: against the committed code, sequential replay returns 200 then 401; 5 concurrent replays return exactly one 200 and four 401; whitespace and url-encoded variants return 401. Mechanism: LoginTokenStore.consume (src/auth/login-tokens.ts) looks up the SHA-256 hash and deletes it in the same synchronous block before the route ever calls sessions.create, so a token can only ever be consumed once. Added tests in tests/auth/single-use.test.ts (commit c1aff25) that spy on the real SessionStore.create and assert it is called exactly once across 5 sequential replays and across 5 concurrent replays, and that only one response carries a session cookie. Note: with `npm start` the emailed token is not retrievable over HTTP (MemoryEmailSender is in-process), so a manual test must run in-process via createApp(); exact repro steps were requested via relay_report_blocker.

AC-4.note: Only tests/auth/single-use.test.ts changed in this repair. Branch diff vs main still touches only src/app.ts, src/auth/**, tests/auth/**. src/server.ts deliberately left untouched (a server-entry replay test was dropped because it would have required editing out-of-scope code).

AC-5.note: npx vitest run: 9 files, 46 tests passed. npm run typecheck clean.

submission.summary: Repair attempt for AC-3. Investigation showed the token replay cannot be reproduced on this branch: consume-and-delete happens atomically before any session is created, and sequential, concurrent, and mutated replays all return 401 after the first 200. Added two regression tests (commit c1aff25) that count real SessionStore.create calls under sequential and concurrent replay and assert exactly one session and one Set-Cookie. No production code changed in this repair because no defect was found; unchanged_scope untouched. Full suite 46/46, typecheck clean. Requested reviewer repro steps via blocker.
